# Python API

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_docs.py from the docstrings and Params fields of wgsextract_cli.api; do not edit. -->

The typed Python API of WGS Extract.

Every operation takes a frozen `*Params` dataclass and returns a
`Result` (the `wgsextract.result/1` manifest model the CLI writes):

```python
from pathlib import Path
from wgsextract_cli import api

res = api.vcf.snp(api.VcfSnpParams(input=Path("x.cram"), region="chrM"))
res.outputs, res.metrics, res.warnings
```

Operations raise `CommandFailed` (carrying the failed `Result`) unless
called with `check=False`. They accept a `progress` callback and a
`CancelToken`. Operations run one at a time per process. They write the same
output files and manifests as the CLI but print nothing to stdout: their
human-readable text is suppressed and external tools' stdout goes to stderr.
Stdout itself is left alone, so the caller's own writes (including from a
progress callback or other threads) still reach it, e.g. a stdio JSON-RPC server.

Unset fields with a config.toml setting take it, as on the CLI. The user's
config.toml is loaded on the first call; `use_config(path)` selects another.

The CLI is built on this layer: each migrated command's options are generated
from its Params fields, so the API and `--help` cannot drift.

Stability: the names exported here and the group modules (`api.extract`,
`api.info`, `api.vcf`, `api.lineage`, `api.microarray`, `api.report`,
`api.sample`, `api.support`) follow semantic versioning from the 1.0
release; adding fields with defaults is not a breaking change.
Modules whose names start with `_` are private and may change at any time.
See docs/api.md.

## Results, progress and cancellation

`api.Result` is the `CommandResult` model of the [result manifest](result-manifest.md): `status`, `exit_code`, `error`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `metrics`, `warnings`, `details`, `manifest` and `provenance`; `to_dict()` and `to_json()` give the `wgsextract.result/1` document. `api.json_schema(cls)` gives a JSON Schema of a Params class; `wgsextract help --all --json` includes it as each typed command's `input_schema`, with each property's flag as `x-cli-flag`.

### `api.ProgressEvent`

One progress report: a stage name, a message and, when known, how far
through the operation is (0.0 to 1.0).

Stages so far: `start` and `finish` (the command name, 0.0 and
1.0), `tool` (an external tool is starting), `step` (a resumable
workflow runs or skips one of its steps, and why) and `heartbeat` (a
periodic count from a long tool run, such as `"1,200/5,000 reads"`, with
the fraction of that run done when the total is known). More stages may be
added.

### `api.ProgressCallback`

Receives progress events, from the calling thread or a worker thread.

### `api.CancelToken`

Cooperative cancellation of a running operation.

`cancel()` may be called from any thread. It stops the operation's
external tools at once and makes the operation fail as cancelled at its
next checkpoint. A token belongs to one operation.

- `is_set`: Alias of `cancelled`, so a token works where a `threading.Event` does.
- `on_cancel`: Call `callback` on cancellation (at once if already cancelled); returns a function that unregisters it.

### `api.CommandFailed`

An operation failed; `result` holds the error, warnings and partial outputs.

## `api.info`

`info`: what a BAM/CRAM is (build, sequencer, sex, depth) and its coverage;
`info chip`: which microarray chip a raw-data file came from.

### `api.info.info(InfoParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info`.

Describe a BAM/CRAM.

`details` holds the metrics (`ref_model_str`, `gender`,
`sequencer`, `avg_read_len`, `metrics`, ...); `metrics` holds the
headline numbers.

`InfoParams`: Identify the reference build, file integrity and sequencing metrics of a
BAM/CRAM. Metrics are cached next to the outputs as
`<input>.wgse_info.json`.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `detailed` | `bool` | `False` | `--detailed` | Perform full index and body sample analysis (detailed mode) |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |
| `cache` | `bool` | `True` | `--cache` | Save the metrics as ``<input>.wgse_info.json`` for later runs; an existing cache is read either way. |

### `api.info.calculate_coverage(CalculateCoverageParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info calculate-coverage`.

Exact coverage; outputs the coverage table (or the depth-bins TSV).

`CalculateCoverageParams`: Exact per-chromosome breadth and depth of coverage (`samtools coverage`).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `bins` | `bool` | `False` | `--bins` | Report exact per-contig depth 0, 1-3, 4-7 and 8+ breadth in one streaming pass. |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed; None saves none. With bins, the depth-band table's format instead (None: tsv). One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

### `api.info.coverage_sample(CoverageSampleParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info coverage-sample`.

Sampled coverage estimate; outputs the coverage table.

`CoverageSampleParams`: Estimated per-chromosome breadth of coverage from ~1,000 sampled windows.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to describe. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

### `api.info.chip(ChipParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract info chip`.

Identify a raw-data file's chip; `details` holds the candidates and
`metrics` the best `revision`, `match` and `confidence`.

`ChipParams`: Identify the vendor, chip and revision of a consumer microarray
raw-data file, or list the catalogued revisions.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | Microarray raw-data file; required unless list_revisions. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `list_revisions` | `bool` | `False` | `--list` | List the catalogued chip revisions and their matching templates. |

## `api.extract`

`extract`: pull chromosomes, regions or unmapped reads out of a BAM/CRAM
into smaller BAM, VCF or FASTA files.

Outputs are named after the input (`sample.bam` gives `sample_Y.bam`) and
written to `outdir`, else beside the input. Calling and consensus commands
(`mito_fasta`, `mito_vcf`, `ydna_vcf`) need the matching reference; the
others use it only to decode a CRAM.

### `api.extract.mito_fasta(MitoFastaParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract extract mito-fasta`.

Write the mitochondrial consensus FASTA (output role `mt_fasta`).

`MitoFastaParams`: The mitochondrial consensus sequence as `<input>_MT.fasta`: chrM
reads called haploid with bcftools and applied to the reference's chrM.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to extract from. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `memory` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `memory_limit`) | `--memory`, `-m` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. '2G'; None picks a share of this machine's RAM (default: config memory_limit, else auto). |

### `api.extract.mito_vcf(MitoVcfParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract extract mito-vcf`.

Call mitochondrial variants (output role `mt_vcf`; the `variants`
metric counts them).

`MitoVcfParams`: Mitochondrial variants as `<input>_MT.vcf.gz`, called haploid.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |

CLI: `wgsextract extract bam-subset`.

## `api.vcf`

`vcf snp` / `vcf indel`: small-variant calling with bcftools.

### `api.vcf.snp(VcfSnpParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract vcf snp`.

Call SNPs; the `snps` output carries the record count in its metrics.

`VcfSnpParams`: Call SNPs from a BAM/CRAM into `snps.vcf.gz`.

Ploidy comes from `ploidy` or `ploidy_file`, else the reference
library's ploidy file, else bcftools' built-in GRCh37/GRCh38 table.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM or CRAM to call. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `ploidy_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy-file` | File defining ploidy per chromosome (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `ploidy` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy` | Predefined ploidy name or value |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `parallel` | `bool` | `False` | `--parallel` | Call contigs in parallel with up to --threads workers. SNP calling then recalls the stretches with sites deeper than 255 reads in one stream, because bcftools subsamples them with one random stream per process, so the calls match the default single stream. |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

SNP calling then recalls the stretches with sites deeper than 255 reads in one stream, because bcftools subsamples them with one random stream per process, so the calls match the default single stream. |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

## `api.lineage`

`lineage`: mtDNA haplogroups (Haplogrep), Y haplogroups (native Yleaf)
and Y-STR repeat counts.

### `api.lineage.mt_haplogroup(MtHaplogroupParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage mt-haplogroup`.

mtDNA haplogroup; `metrics` holds `haplogroup` and
`haplogroup_quality`, `details["haplogrep"]` the full Haplogrep row.

`MtHaplogroupParams`: Predict the mtDNA haplogroup with Haplogrep from a BAM/CRAM (chrM is
called first; needs the reference) or a VCF. The report is
`haplogrep_results.txt` in the output folder.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF with chrM/MT. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `haplogrep_path` | `str \| None` | `None` (config `haplogrep_executable`) | `--haplogrep-path` | Path to haplogrep executable or JAR (optional if in PATH) |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

### `api.lineage.y_haplogroup(YHaplogroupParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage y-haplogroup`.

Y haplogroup; `metrics` holds `haplogroup`, `haplogroup_marker` and
`qc_score`, `details["predictions"]` every Yleaf prediction row.

`YHaplogroupParams`: Predict the Y haplogroup with the bundled native Yleaf from a BAM, CRAM
or single-sample VCF/BCF. Outputs go to `yleaf/` in the output folder.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or single-sample VCF/BCF. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `pos_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--pos-file` | Yleaf position file (optional) |
| `build` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--build` | Override the detected reference build for this run. One of: `hg19`, `hg38`, `t2t` |
| `tree` | `str` | `'yfull'` | `--tree` | Yleaf v4.1.6 haplogroup tree (default: yfull). One of: `yfull`, `yfull_v10`, `ftdna`, `isogg` |
| `min_reads` | `int` | `10` | `--min-reads` | Reads needed at a marker position for it to be used. |
| `base_quality` | `int` | `20` | `--base-quality` | Minimum base quality of a read at a marker position. |
| `base_majority` | `int` | `90` | `--base-majority` | Percentage of reads at a marker that must agree on the base. |
| `min_score` | `float` | `0.95` | `--min-score` | Minimum QC score of a reported haplogroup prediction. |
| `ancient` | `bool` | `False` | `--ancient` | Use ancient-DNA marker tables. |
| `no_ref_inference` | `bool` | `False` | `--no-ref-inference` | VCF: use genotyped positions only (targeted panels); otherwise --ref is required. |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

### `api.lineage.y_str(YStrParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract lineage y-str`.

Y-STR calls; `details["calls"]` lists every marker with its value and
read support.

`YStrParams`: Call Y-STR repeat counts from a BAM/CRAM into `ystr/` (a table and a
FamilyTreeDNA-order CSV).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | Indexed BAM or CRAM. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `panel` | `str` | `'Y-111'` | `--panel` | Marker panel: FamilyTreeDNA Y-12 to Y-111, PowerPlex Y23, Yfiler Plus, or all (default: Y-111). One of: `Y-12`, `Y-25`, `Y-37`, `Y-67`, `Y-111`, `PPY23`, `YfilerPlus`, `all` |
| `build` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--build` | Override the detected reference build for this run. One of: `hg19`, `hg38`, `t2t` |
| `min_reads` | `int` | `2` | `--min-reads` | Spanning reads needed to support a repeat count (default: 2). |
| `min_fraction` | `float` | `0.6` | `--min-fraction` | Share of spanning reads that must agree (default: 0.6). |
| `min_mapq` | `int` | `20` | `--min-mapq` | Minimum mapping quality for single-copy markers (default: 20). |

## `api.microarray`

`microarray`: consumer microarray (23andMe, AncestryDNA, ...) and AADR
files generated from a BAM/CRAM or VCF.

### `api.microarray.generate(MicroarrayParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract microarray`.

Generate the kits; each output carries its marker tallies in `metrics`.

`MicroarrayParams`: Generate a combined 23andMe-style kit and the selected vendor or AADR
formats from a BAM, CRAM or VCF.

Fields left at `None` fall back to config.toml (`microarray_*`
settings) and then to the documented default.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path` | required | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF to genotype. |
| `ref` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `reference_fasta`) | `--ref` | Reference FASTA or reference library folder; resolved from the input's header when omitted (default: config reference_fasta). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the input's folder). |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` (config `cpu_threads`) | `--threads`, `-t` | CPU threads; None picks a count for this machine (default: config cpu_threads, else auto). |
| `formats` | `str` | `'all'` | `--formats` | Comma-separated formats to generate, e.g. "23andme_v5,ancestry_v2" (default: "all", the combined kit only); see `wgsextract microarray --help` for the list. |
| `table_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--format` | Also save the genotypes as <input>_genotypes.tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow): rsID, chrom, pos (in the input's build) and genotype. None saves no table. One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |
| `indel_manifest` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | `--indel-manifest` | Opt-in sequence-defined I/D probes from a matching GRCh37 Illumina CSV, gzip or ZIP; repeat per selected format |
| `strand_ambiguous` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--strand-ambiguous` | Keep/no-call biallelic A/T or C/G input SNPs; unknown probe alleles are not inferred (default: config or keep) One of: `keep`, `no-call` |
| `resolve_rsids` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--resolve-rsids` | Resolve packaged dbSNP aliases and no-call retired/ambiguous marker IDs (default: config or false) |
| `quirks` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--quirks` | corrected: forward-strand calls; vendor: reverse-strand calls where a template's vendor revision reported them so (default: config or corrected) One of: `corrected`, `vendor` |
| `min_gq` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--min-gq` | Minimum sample GQ; missing GQ becomes a no-call (default: config or 0, disabled) |
| `min_dp` | `int \| None` | `None` | `--min-dp` | Minimum sample DP; missing DP becomes a no-call (default: config or 0, disabled) |
| `assume_hom_ref` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--assume-hom-ref` | Assume absent VCF markers are reference on represented contigs (default: config or true) |
| `exclude_filtered` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--exclude-filtered` | No-call VCF records failing FILTER (default: config or false) |
| `call_reasons` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--call-reasons` | Also write CombinedKit_reasons.tsv with explicit reasons (default: config or false) |
| `aadr_sample_id` | `str` | `'sample'` | `--aadr-sample-id` | Non-identifying sample label for AADR .fam/.ind (default: sample) |
| `aadr_sex` | `str` | `'U'` | `--aadr-sex` | AADR metadata sex only; does not change genotype calling (default: U) One of: `U`, `M`, `F` |
| `parallel` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `--parallel` | Call chromosomes in parallel workers (default: on with --threads above 1; calls are identical to one stream) |
| `ref_vcf_tab` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ref-vcf-tab` | Master tabulated list of all consumer microarray SNPs (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `ploidy_file` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--ploidy-file` | File defining ploidy per chromosome (auto-resolved from --ref if possible) |
| `sample` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sample` | Sample to use from a multi-sample VCF (e.g. a joint-called nf-core/sarek VCF); required when the VCF has more than one |
| `region` | `str \| None` | `None` | `-r`, `--region` | Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000) |
| `qc_min_depth` | `float \| None` | `None` | `--qc-min-depth` | Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA) |

## `api.report`

`report`: a sample's results as one local HTML, Markdown and JSON report.

The report summarises what earlier runs left in the sample folder (their
result manifests and the sample workspace): overview and QC, lineage,
pharmacogenomics, ClinVar pathogenic calls in the ACMG SF genes and the
microarray export. It runs no analysis and makes no network calls:

```python
res = api.report.build(api.ReportParams(workspace=Path("HG002")))
report = res.details          # the wgsextract.report/1 document
```

Every finding has a confidence label, its evidence (file relative to the
sample folder, plus region) and the "technical result, not diagnosis"
disclaimer. See docs/personal-report.md.

### `api.report.build(ReportParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract report`.

Write the report. `details` is the `wgsextract.report/1` document;
`outputs` are the HTML (`report_html`), Markdown
(`report_markdown`), JSON (`report_json`) and findings table
(`findings_table`).

`ReportParams`: Summarise a sample's results as <sample>_personal_report.html, .md and .json
plus a findings table, from the result manifests in its folder.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample: only its runs (and runs on files made from it) are reported. Its folder holds the results unless workspace is given. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder whose results are reported (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` (config `output_directory`) | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder for the outputs (default: config output_directory, else the sample folder). |
| `results` | `tuple[Path, ...]` | `[]` | `--results` | Also read result manifests from this folder (repeatable); only runs on this sample's files are used. The --outdir is always read. |
| `table_format` | `str` | `'tsv'` | `--format` | Format of the findings table, <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow) (default: tsv) One of: `tsv`, `parquet` |

## `api.sample`

`sample`: show and correct what is recorded about a sample in its
workspace, `wgsextract.sample.toml` (see docs/sample-workspace.md).

### `api.sample.show(SampleShowParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample show`.

Read the workspace. `details` holds `genome_folder`, the
folder-wide `overrides`, `files` (each recorded file's `status` —
current, changed or missing — its detected `facts` and its own
`overrides` with their `status` and `values`),
`outputs` and, with an input, `effective`: the facts in effect for it,
each with its `source` (override or detected).

`SampleShowParams`: Show a sample's overrides, the facts recorded for each of its files and
the result manifests indexed in its workspace.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |

### `api.sample.set_overrides(SampleSetParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample set`.

Set overrides; `details` is the workspace afterwards, as `show`.

`SampleSetParams`: Set overrides: facts commands use instead of what they detect. A sex
override is folder-wide in a genome folder (one person's files); anything
else, and every platform override, is for the `input` file alone and
lapses when that file changes. Commands still detect an overridden fact
cheaply and warn when the reads disagree.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `sex` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--sex` | The sample's sex (m and f are accepted too); for the whole genome folder, else for --input only. One of: `Male`, `Female` |
| `platform` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--platform` | The sequencing platform of --input (nanopore, hifi, mgi and bgi are accepted too). One of: `illumina`, `ont`, `pacbio`, `ultima`, `dnbseq` |

### `api.sample.unset_overrides(SampleUnsetParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract sample unset`.

Remove overrides; `details` is the workspace afterwards, as `show`.

`SampleUnsetParams`: Remove overrides, so commands detect those facts again: the
folder-wide one and, with `input`, that file's own.

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--input`, `-i` | BAM, CRAM or VCF of the sample; its folder is the workspace unless workspace is given, and its facts are shown. |
| `workspace` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--workspace` | Sample folder holding wgsextract.sample.toml (default: the --genome folder, else the --input's folder). |
| `sex` | `bool` | `False` | `--sex` | Remove the sex override. |
| `platform` | `bool` | `False` | `--platform` | Remove the platform override. |

## `api.support`

`report-issue`: a pre-filled, redacted GitHub bug report.

`build_issue_report` collects this installation's versions, OS, CPU, RAM,
tools and settings and, by default, the last run recorded on this computer
(command line, exit status, error, warnings, log tail), redacts them, and
fits them into a GitHub new-issue link:

```python
report = api.support.build_issue_report(api.ReportIssueParams(last_failed=True))
print(report.body)                     # review it
api.support.open_issue(report)         # the user submits it on GitHub
```

Nothing is uploaded: the link opens GitHub's new-issue form in the browser,
where the user reviews and submits it. Reports never contain genotypes, reads,
file contents, sample, user or computer names, full paths or secrets.

### `api.support.build_issue_report(ReportIssueParams)`

CLI: `wgsextract report-issue`.

Collect, redact and fit a report; writes nothing and opens nothing.

`result` reports on that run (e.g. one the API just returned) instead of
`params.run` or the last recorded run. Raises `UsageError` when
`params.run` is not a readable manifest, run log or provenance file.

`ReportIssueParams`: Build a redacted GitHub bug report about this installation and a run
(by default the last one recorded on this computer).

| Field | Type | Default | CLI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--run` | Report on this run: a result manifest (*.manifest.json), a run log (*.log) or its *.provenance.json (default: the last run). |
| `last_failed` | `bool` | `False` | `--last-failed` | Report on the last failed run instead of the last run. |
| `title` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--title` | Issue title (default: the command and its exit code; the error goes in the body). |
| `description` | `str \| None` | `None` | `--description` | What you did and what went wrong, for the 'What happened?' field. |
| `log_lines` | `int` | `40` | `--log-lines` | Log lines to include, from the end (default: 40). |
| `max_url_length` | `int` | `8000` | `--max-url-length` | Longest link to produce; diagnostics are shortened to fit (default: 8000; at least 1000). |
| `outdir` | `Path \| None` | `None` | `--outdir`, `-o` | Folder to save the full report in (default: 'reports' in the per-user data folder). |

### `api.support.reports_directory() -> Path`

Where reports are saved by default: `reports` in the state directory
(the `state_directory` setting, else `state` in the data folder).

### `api.support.issue_url(report: IssueReport, *, max_length: int = 8000) -> str`

The new-issue link for `report` after editing its `title`,
`description` or `link_diagnostics` (`dataclasses.replace`); the
diagnostics are cut at a line if the link would exceed `max_length`.

### `api.support.save_issue_report(report: IssueReport, directory: Path | None = None) -> Path`

Save the full redacted report (`report.body`) as Markdown in
`directory` (default: `reports` in the per-user data folder).

### `api.support.open_issue(report: IssueReport) -> bool`

Open `report.url` in the browser; False when no browser could start.
Only call this after the user has seen the report and agreed.

### `api.support.IssueReport`

A redacted bug report, ready to show the user and open on GitHub.

`diagnostics` is the full redacted text, saved locally by
`save`; `link_diagnostics` is what fits in `url` (see
`truncated`). Edit `title`, `description` or `link_diagnostics`
with `dataclasses.replace` and call `issue_url` for a new link.

- `body`: The whole issue as Markdown, as saved in the diagnostics file.
- `save`: Write `body` to `directory/file_name` (readable only by the user).
